# Ops / SRE & Phase 0 Closure Gate — Domain Agent 6

**Repo root:** `/Users/mohamed/syncfs`  
**Date:** 2026-11-08  
**Scope:** `README.md`, `.spec/state.md`, `.spec/roadmap.md`, `.spec/tasks.md`, `docs/operating-model.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `.spec/technical_spec.md` §§10,12,13,14, `.spec/research.md`, stale docs `.spec/consensus-layer.md`, `.spec/directory-replication-daemon.md`, `arch/architecture-proposal.md`, `docs/directory-daemon.md`.  
**Instruction honoured:** Do NOT edit spec files. This file is the only write. All verdicts cite a primary URL. Excerpts are short verbatim quotes; full pages should be re-fetched for audit.

**Method:** Read local docs, then fetch primary sources: etcd metrics/monitoring/clustering/learner/robustness, CockroachDB metrics/start, Prometheus exposition/histograms/alerting, SRE Book Ch.6/10, systemd.service(5), NIST SP 800-57 Pt.1, HashiCorp Vault/Consul, Ceph add/remove mons, Jepsen, Atlassian Jira/Confluence DC, JFrog Artifactory HA. Where etcd.io returned navigation boilerplate, excerpts are taken from the etcd GitHub robustness README, the CockroachDB metrics table, and the Prometheus/systemd man-page mirror — all primary.

**Unified baseline (fork closed 2026-11-08, `research/07-design-fork-reconciliation.md` §3.5 + D-001):** This audit does **not** re-litigate the data-path fork. MVP = **Camp A data path**: FUSE mount + `go.etcd.io/etcd/raft/v3` + QUIC+mTLS push/pipeline + Pebble/BLAKE3 strict volume + learner-first admission. `hashicorp/raft`, watcher-based mutation path, pull-based steady-state transport, per-directory epoch fencing, and per-directory async modes are **SUPERSEDED for MVP** (post-MVP tiers only). Camp B contributions **ADOPTED into MVP**: node-state taxonomy (LEADER/FOLLOWER/FENCED/CANDIDATE/CATCHING_UP/QUARANTINED/HALTED), quarantine discipline, POSIX-apply vectors (chown-before-chmod, ACL/xattr/symlink/hardlink/mtime, CAP_CHOWN, uid/gid consistency), witness/learner vocabulary. Fencing token = Raft committed **term/index** (not per-directory epoch). Banners in §3 are harmonized to the exact D-001 texts in 07 §4. **No D-001 challenge from the Ops/SRE domain:** the baseline is operable provided the gate in §4 closes (observability catalog, join interlocks, fault matrix). Specific Ops implications are flagged inline with `D-001:`.

Copy the metric names in rows A1–A4 as `syncfs_*` counterparts.

**Answer to Q2:** SyncFS enrollment bundle (offline CA + pre-authorized fingerprint + one-time nonce + mTLS seed + verified snapshot + chunk scrub + joint consensus + drain-old-last) is **stronger than etcd/CockroachDB/Ceph/Consul/Vault** on identity. Missing interlocks: (1) data-dir-empty + format/cluster-ID/version match pre-flight, (2) advertise-address + disk-space + clock-offset + version-skew checks, (3) bootstrap-disable step + server-side `volume apply` refusal until 3 healthy voters, (4) stabilization timer + trailing-log + last-contact thresholds, (5) dead-learner cleanup with `min_quorum` guard, (6) quorum-verify command before demoting old voter, (7) IP immutability (Ceph) + dedicated-host rule.

**Answer to Q3:** `tasks.md` M4-04 + §13 + §3.8 is **narrower than etcd robustness and Jepsen**. Present: kill, pause, partition, delay/dup, disk-full, corrupt-pack, FUSE-restart, learner-interruption, daemon-restart-at-each-boundary (good). Missing: (1) model/linearizability validator + report artifacts, (2) compaction/snapshot/defrag/GC/pack-seal **during** traffic crashes, (3) slow-disk/stall (not full), (4) clock skew/jump, (5) silent bit-rot, (6) cert expiry mid-transaction, (7) thundering-herd on failover, (8) mount SIGSTOP vs kill, (9) duplicate/retry storm, (10) long soak (hours–days) + independent Jepsen-style audit. The stale lease doc’s clock-jump + crash-vs-hang + ExecStopPost-EBUSY caveats should be mined, not lost.

| D7 | JFrog Artifactory HA: 2+ nodes same LAN, 3 for true HA + no-downtime upgrades; external DB mandatory (Derby forbidden); shared storage + LB + N app nodes; file-system redundancy > N/2 | Open Q1; §5.1 | https://docs.jfrog.com/installation/docs/high-availability | “You can configure JFrog services for High Availability (HA) with a cluster of **two or more nodes on the same Local Area Network (LAN)**.” + “For full resilience and no-downtime upgrades, use a minimum of three nodes.” + “You must use an **external database**… You cannot use high availability with the in-built Derby database.” | **SPEC MISSES ANALOGUE.** SyncFS needs: “3 storage voters same LAN, RTT <1 ms, no WAN” (not just “low-latency”), “no local-only state dir counted as quorum”, and chunk redundancy **> N/2** (already quorum 2/3, but state explicitly as JFrog does). |
| D8 | JFrog storage: default `file-system` replication across nodes; external blob still needs PVC or pods lose data on crash | Open Q1; §7 | https://docs.jfrog.com/installation/docs/artifactory-storage | “The default is `file-system` replication, which replicates data across all nodes.” + “When using external blob storage … a PVC … is still required … Skipping the PVC can cause data loss on unplanned pod termination.” | **SYNCFS ANALOGUE MISSING.** `packs/` on local ext4/XFS is SyncFS’s filestore. State: “if `/var/lib/syncfs` is wiped, node rejoins as learner and must re-sync; never count wiped node toward quorum” + PVC-equivalent “do not share state dir across voters”. |

**Answer to Q4:** Open question 1 (“which exact app/version?”) cannot be closed with just a name. Atlassian/JFrog prove qualification must pin **five** things SyncFS currently omits: (1) **same-path + generously-sized + growth-plan** shared home, (2) **matched nodes + ntpd + same region/LAN + no multicast**, (3) **local vs shared split** (index/log/config vs attachments), (4) **LB affinity + least-connections + `/status` semantics + drain**, (5) **split-brain panic + heartbeat-vs-integrity tuning** (Confluence ClusterSafetyJob/Hazelcast). M5-02 must capture each as a test, not only “vendor test suite passes”. Confluence S3-attachments and JFrog Derby-ban are useful negatives: SyncFS must state “no S3 backend in MVP; no local-only quorum” explicitly.

### E. systemd, cert rotation, Prometheus ops (cross-cutting)

| # | Claim | Spec ref | URL | Excerpt | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | systemd long-running services should use `Type=notify` (sd_notify READY) and `Restart=on-failure`; `Type=simple` reports success before binary runs | Tasks M4-03; operating-model mount ordering | https://manpages.debian.org/testing/systemd/systemd.service.5.en.html | “If set to **simple** … the service manager will consider the unit started immediately after the main service process has been forked off … before the new process has called **execve()**…” + “Setting this to **on-failure** is the recommended choice for long-running services…” | **SPEC MISSING.** M4-03 says “systemd units” with no `Type=`, `Restart=`, `TimeoutStartSec`. Require `Type=notify` (daemon + mount send READY after quorum/lease ready), `Restart=on-failure`, `RestartSec`, `TimeoutStartSec`. |
| E2 | `ExecStopPost` runs even on failed start; `ExecStop` does not; restart is stop+start so both run on restart | §10; stale docs’ fence note | https://manpages.debian.org/testing/systemd/systemd.service.5.en.html | “Note that the commands specified in *ExecStop=* are only executed when the service started successfully first… Use *ExecStopPost=* to invoke commands when a service failed to start up correctly…” + “Service restart requests are implemented as stop operations followed by start operations.” | **STALE DOC CORRECT, NORMATIVE SPEC SILENT.** `.spec/directory-replication-daemon.md`’s EBUSY/`ExecStopPost` best-effort note is accurate per E2, but normative spec has no fence-on-stop story. Move it to §10: FUSE `remount,ro` may EBUSY; `ExecStopPost` fence is best-effort; epoch check on replicas is backstop. |
| E3 | Watchdog needs periodic `WATCHDOG=1` keep-alive; TimeoutStopSec escalates SIGTERM→SIGKILL | M4-03; `architecture.md` mount failure row | https://manpages.debian.org/testing/systemd/systemd.service.5.en.html | “The service must call sd_notify(3) regularly with ‘WATCHDOG=1’ … If the time between two such calls is larger … then the service is placed in a failed state and it will be terminated with SIGABRT…” + “If it does not terminate in the specified time, it will be forcibly terminated by SIGKILL.” | **SPEC MISSING.** Add `WatchdogSec=` (e.g. 30 s) for daemon (heartbeat to leader) + mount (FUSE liveness), `TimeoutStopSec=` (e.g. 10 s) + `KillMode`. Without watchdog a hung mount serving stale cache is invisible. |
| E4 | NIST key management covers cryptoperiod, rotation-before-compromise, archive/destroy, inventory, protection | §9; operating-model cert row | https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/57/pt1/r5/final | Abstract: “provides general guidance and best practices for the management of cryptographic keying material, including definitions of the security services… specifications of the protection that each type of key … requires…” (full PDF defines cryptoperiod/rotation/archive/destroy phases). | **SPEC INSUFFICIENT.** Operating-model cert row (“add new, verify, remove old”) lacks cryptoperiod, overlap window, inventory, CA-key protection/backup, revocation. See gate §5 for exact NIST-aligned runbook. |
| E5 | CockroachDB cert-expiry + auth are observable (`security.certificate.expiration.*` + cipher allowlist log) | §9; §12.3 | https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.2/metrics | `security.certificate.expiration.ca`, `security.certificate.expiration.node` (“Expiration timestamp in seconds since Unix epoch… 0 means no certificate or error.”) | **SYNCFS PARTIAL.** §12.3 lists “certificate expiry” but not both CA + node/client gauges, nor cipher-suite rejection counter. Add `syncfs_cert_expiry_seconds{kind=ca|node|client}` + `syncfs_tls_handshake_rejected_total{reason}`; alert at 30 d (ticket) + 7 d (page). |

## 2. Synthesis — direct answers to the five questions

1. **Observability:** No. See §1A. Adopt CockroachDB/etcd metric names as `syncfs_*` counterparts, add golden signals, Prometheus exposition/cardinality rules, and symptom-based alerting with durations + runbooks. Without this M4-03 cannot be verified.
2. **Bootstrap/join:** Enrollment bundle + learner-first is sound and stronger than all four HA systems on identity. Add the seven interlocks in §1B (pre-flight checks, bootstrap-disable, stabilization/trailing-log/last-contact, dead-learner `min_quorum`, quorum-verify, IP/dedicated-host rules). M4-02 needs those thresholds as explicit tasks.
3. **Fault matrix:** M4-04 is a starting point, not parity with etcd robustness/Jepsen. Add model checker, compaction/defrag/GC-crash coverage, slow-disk, clock-skew, bit-rot, cert-expiry-mid-txn, thundering-herd, SIGSTOP, retry-storm, and long soak (see §1C). §13 needs a consistency-model declaration + report artifact.
4. **App qualification:** Open Q1 must be closed as a five-part contract (same-path, matched/ntpd/same-LAN, local-vs-shared, LB/health/drain, split-brain/heartbeat tuning) per Atlassian + JFrog, not just a product name. M5-02 test list must enumerate each; `docs/compatibility.md` must not claim “Jira/Confluence supported” until then.
5. **Phase 0 closure:** Foundation cannot be “Done” today. See gate §4: docs are internally contradictory (stale Raft/no-FUSE files still present without banners), no version pins, no reproducible `go test` evidence, open questions have no defaults, link-audit has no log. Honest close requires gate items G1–G28 all checked with command output attached.

## 5. Concrete corrections proposed (do not apply to spec files yet) — D-001 aligned

**D-001 alignment:** Corrections below assume the unified baseline (§3.5). They fold in Camp B’s adopted contributions — node-state taxonomy LEADER/FOLLOWER/FENCED/CANDIDATE/CATCHING_UP/QUARANTINED/HALTED as operability states over Raft+receipt state, quarantine discipline for staged-but-unreferenced chunks, POSIX-apply vectors as acceptance tests, witness/learner vocabulary — and they do **not** reintroduce hashicorp/raft, watcher mutation path, pull-based steady-state, epoch fencing, or per-directory async modes for MVP. Fencing token is stated everywhere as Raft committed term/index (07 §3.5). If a future async tier needs those, it requires a new decision + separate contract (D-001 Consequences).

### 5.1 `docs/operating-model.md`

1. **Replace §Required observability (L107-123) with a metric catalog table.** Columns: Metric | Type | Labels | Buckets/Threshold | Severity | Runbook. Minimum rows (names are proposals; keep `syncfs_` prefix):
   - `syncfs_raft_leader_info{volume}` (gauge 0/1), `syncfs_raft_quorum_ok` (gauge), `syncfs_raft_term`
   - `syncfs_raft_proposals_pending`, `syncfs_raft_log_behind_entries{peer}`, `syncfs_raft_applied_lag_seconds` (histogram), `syncfs_raft_commit_latency_seconds` (histogram), `syncfs_raft_apply_latency_seconds`
   - `syncfs_disk_wal_fsync_duration_seconds` (histogram, buckets 1/5/10/25/50/100 ms), `syncfs_disk_pack_fsync_duration_seconds`, `syncfs_disk_available_bytes` + `syncfs_disk_fill_hours`
   - `syncfs_clock_offset_nanoseconds`, `syncfs_process_open_fds`, `syncfs_go_goroutines`, `syncfs_snapshot_{send,recv}_{inflight,queue}`
   - `syncfs_operations_total{operation,result,errno}`, `syncfs_operation_latency_seconds{operation,phase}` (histogram), `syncfs_lease_revocation_wait_seconds`, `syncfs_lock_wait_seconds`, `syncfs_operation_ambiguous_total`
   - `syncfs_chunk_checksum_failures_total`, `syncfs_repair_backlog`, `syncfs_gc_backlog`, `syncfs_cert_expiry_seconds{kind=ca|node|client}`
   - `syncfs_membership_changes_total`, `syncfs_enrollment_events_total`, `syncfs_admin_audit_total`
   Add: alphabet of labels, cardinality budget (“≤200 series per histogram; `operation`/`phase` only; `node_id` on gauges, not histograms”), recording rules for p99 (`histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(...)))`), and Prometheus exposition note (base-unit seconds, `+Inf` bucket).
2. **Add symptom/cause alert table.** Page: quorum loss, write-error rate >1% (5 m), p99 >25 ms (5 m), cert expiry <7 d, clock offset >250 ms, single-voter disk >85%. Ticket: single-voter disk >70%, learner lag >1000 entries, proposals_pending >100 (5 m), GC/repair backlog growing (1 h), cert expiry <30 d. Every alert has `for:` + `runbook: docs/operations/runbooks/<name>.md` + dashboard link. Add metamonitoring (`up`, `ALERTS` firing, Prometheus/Alertmanager health).
3. **Expand Bootstrap and volume lifecycle with interlocks.** After the CLI block, add:
   - **Pre-flight (daemon refuses to bootstrap/join):** data-dir empty-or-claimed, `ClusterID` + `FormatVersion` match bundle, binary version == cluster version, advertise address reachable, free space ≥ snapshot + 20%, clock offset <250 ms (ntpd required), `initial-cluster-state` semantics documented.
   - **Bootstrap-disable:** `syncfs admin cluster bootstrap --seed node-a` puts control plane in `bootstrap: true`; the server must refuse `volume apply` until `voters==3 && all healthy && appliedIndex==commitIndex` for `server_stabilization_time` (default 30 s), then operator runs `… bootstrap --close` (or auto-close after stabilization + explicit confirm). Never accept local YAML edits as authority (already stated; keep).
   - **Learner promotion gate:** learner must show `applied==commit`, scrub OK, trailing logs ≤1000, last-contact <10 s for 30 s, then joint-consensus promote. Dead-learner cleanup: `dead_server_last_contact_threshold` (default 24 h) must exceed snapshot-load time; `min_quorum=2` (never prune below quorum).
   - **Replacement:** add-new-first, verify quorum, drain old, remove last (already stated; add `syncfs admin cluster status` quorum-verify command + “never inject/rotate certs while daemon stopped-then-manually-injected” Ceph lesson).
4. **Expand Recovery table with cert rotation + clock + systemd.** Replace the one-line cert row with a 5-step runbook citing NIST SP 800-57: (i) set cryptoperiod (node 90 d, CA 1 y), (ii) issue new node certs + trust bundle to all voters, (iii) rolling reload (`SIGHUP`/notify-reload; no restart), (iv) verify every peer handshakes with new cert, (v) committed removal of old material + audit. Add rows: clock offset >250 ms → fence + page; slow-disk (fsync >1 s) → `syncfs_disk_stall_total` + page; mount SIGSTOP → socket watchdog + abort FUSE connection.
5. **Add systemd unit template + mount ordering.** `syncfs daemon` and `syncfs mount` units: `Type=notify`, `Restart=on-failure`, `RestartSec=2s`, `TimeoutStartSec=30s`, `TimeoutStopSec=10s`, `WatchdogSec=30s` (daemon pings leader-lease; mount pings FUSE-lease), `ExecStopPost` fence note with EBUSY caveat (E2). Mount unit `Requires=` + `After=` daemon/cluster-health target; app unit `Requires=` + `After=` mount (already prose; make it `Requires=`/`After=` not just “starts before”).
6. **Add deployment prerequisites box.** Same region/LAN, RTT <1 ms, no multicast, 10 GbE + NVMe already stated — add: dedicated hosts (no voter + OSD-equivalent brick on same drive), separate NIC for inter-server where possible, ntpd/chronyd mandatory, same binary version on all voters, FUSE mount path identical on all app hosts.

**D-001 notes:** metrics include `syncfs_node_state{state=LEADER|FOLLOWER|FENCED|CANDIDATE|CATCHING_UP|QUARANTINED|HALTED}`, `syncfs_quarantine_chunks_total`, `syncfs_mass_delete_breaker_trips_total`; fencing is `syncfs_raft_term` (term/index), never epoch. QUIC push/pipeline is steady-state; pull survives only as learner catch-up replay. POSIX-apply vectors (chown-before-chmod etc.) belong in `docs/compatibility.md` as M3-02 tests.

4. **Pin versions in scope.** “Pin a Go 1.25+ Linux toolchain” becomes “Pin Go exactly `<x.y.z>` (e.g. `go 1.25.0` + `toolchain go1.25.0`) on Linux CI; pin etcd `raft/v3 <v>`, quic-go `<v>`, Pebble `<v>`, go-fuse/v2 `<v>` in `go.mod` + `go.sum`; no `@main`.” Until M1-01 lands, state.md must warn “no code may depend on a moving branch” (§6) is aspirational, not yet true.

| Claim (file:line) | What it says | Hard evidence present? | What would make it honest |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tasks.md:18` Foundation `done` | Phase table | **No.** No commit, log, reviewer, or gate link. Contradicted by unbanners stale files (G1.1 fail). | Either uncheck until G1–G6 pass, or append `(evidence: <commit> <commands> <output>)` per box. |
| `tasks.md:39-47` M0-01 `[x]` | “Define topology… failure model… ” | **No.** No diff hash, no link-audit log, docs still contradictory. | Attach `git diff --check` + link-audit output + stale-banner proof (G1.1). |

The fourth box (go tests) is correctly unchecked — that honesty is good and should be kept. | Convert to `[ ]` until G2/G6 evidence exists, or add evidence strings per G6.3. |
| `roadmap.md:18` Milestone 0 `Done` | “Normative spec… exist” | **No.** “Exist” is true; “Done” implies gate passed. No evidence column, no pins, open Qs unresolved. | Downgrade to “Ready to close pending gate” (G6.1) until G1–G6 checked. |
| `state.md:17` Foundation `done` | Milestone table | **No.** Same contradiction as above; verification column says only “Markdown/link review and git diff --check” (process, not result). | Same downgrade; verification must be command outputs, not process names. |

Keep this row as-is; do not “fix” it by claiming pass. | Record `go version` output (=1.15.6) + `ls go.mod` (missing) as evidence. |

**Bottom line:** The only fully honest rows are the two *negative* ones — `go test: Blocked` and “CLI not implemented yet”. Every `done`/`passed` in the tracker is currently a process claim (“we ran a review / ran a check”) without the artifact that would let an independent engineer reproduce it (hash, log, URL, version). Phase 0 is **not** closable in this state. Downgrade the five `done/passed` rows to “ready to close pending gate” and attach evidence per G6.1 before re-checking them.

**D-001 challenge assessment (Ops/SRE): NO CHALLENGE.** No primary-source evidence was found that the unified baseline (§3.5: FUSE + etcd/raft/v3 + QUIC push/pipeline + learner-first + term/index fencing) cannot work. The Ops costs of the baseline — Ready-loop persistence ordering (etcd deterministic core), stall-on-partition (FUSE), learner catch-up throughput — are already priced in §11 SLOs and in gate G5 (metrics/interlocks/fault matrix). Reopening watcher/hashicorp/pull/epoch for MVP would require a new decision revising either the north-star contract or 07 §3.1’s proof (D-001 Consequences). This audit respects that boundary.
